question: Should OpenClaw accept Vault as a bundled plugin whose exec resolver receives Vault auth material and performs Vault network reads, or keep Vault as an external ClawHub/plugin package?
rationale: The implementation uses the shipped SecretRef integration seam, but distribution of a credential-bearing network resolver inside core is a maintainer/security boundary choice that automation should not make.

options.title: Accept bundled after cleanup
options.body: Fix the docs, boundary, and runtime-asset blockers, then land only after secops/dependency approval for the current head.

options.title: Keep Vault external
options.body: Close or pause the bundled PR and ask for the Vault provider to be published as an external ClawHub/plugin package using the existing SecretRef integration contract.

options.title: Narrow to external-plugin docs
options.body: Replace the bundled resolver with documentation and examples showing how external Vault plugins should use the manifest integration seam.

recommendation.title: Accept bundled after cleanup
recommendation.body: Fix the docs, boundary, and runtime-asset blockers, then land only after secops/dependency approval for the current head.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining non-mechanical decision is the bundled security/dependency trust boundary, and he is the best available routing candidate from the security-adjacent history and prior assignment.
